mainTopic: The mourner's bed, the king's powers in the משנה, פרשת מלך, the order of the three מצוות on entering the land, and the fall of שלמה
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining how a דרגש differs from a regular bed. A challenge from a משנה in כלים replaces the first explanation with a new one. It then rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about the mourner's דרגש and adds a rule about beds with tall posts. A new משנה lists the king's powers: an optional war with the approval of the 71, breaking through to make roads, and the first share of the spoils. שמואל and רב, and before them רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה, argue whether the king may really do everything in פרשת מלך. Other ברייתות discuss whether appointing a king is a מצוה, and רבי יוסי proves the order: first a king, then wiping out עמלק, then building the בית המקדש. ריש לקיש describes how שלמה's kingdom shrank step by step, and רב and שמואל argue whether he ever became king again. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה: a ברייתא divides the spoils, and אביי asks for the source, which begins at the end of the amud.

steps.title: How a דרגש and a bed are strung
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן finishes his definition: a דרגש has its straps strung from the inside, while a bed has its straps wrapped over the outside of the frame.
steps.simpleTranslation: A דרגש has its weaving on the inside; a bed has its weaving over its back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי יוחנן's explanation of what makes a דרגש different from an ordinary bed. This matters because a mourner treats a דרגש differently from a regular bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, the difference is where the straps are tied. On a דרגש they go into holes inside the frame. On a bed they wrap around the frame from above, so they cover it.

keyTerms.meaning: The weaving or webbing of straps that holds up the bedding
A special kind of couch or bed that a mourner does not overturn
Over its back, meaning on the outside of the frame

phrases.english: its weaving is on its inside,
phrases.notes: This finishes רבי יוחנן's sentence from just before, and 'its' means the דרגש.

phrases.english: a bed – its weaving is over its back.

steps.triggerLanguage: סֵירוּגוֹ מִתּוֹכוֹ, מִטָּה – סֵירוּגָהּ מֵעַל גַּבָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יוחנן's answer to the earlier question of what a דרגש is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A דרגש is strung from inside the frame; a bed is strung with straps wrapped over the frame.

steps.title: Challenge from the smoothing of beds
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in כלים says a wooden bed can become impure only once it is smoothed with fish skin. If the straps covered the frame, why would smoothing matter?
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: When can wooden vessels become impure? A bed and a crib can become impure once they are smoothed with fish skin. But if a bed is strung over its back, why do I need smoothing with fish skin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's explanation using a משנה about טומאה of wooden vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a bed counts as finished only after its wood is smoothed. If the straps wrapped over the frame and hid it, nobody would bother smoothing it. So the frame must be visible, and that means beds are not strung over the top.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged, which introduces a source that contradicts what was just said
Smoothing the wood with rough fish skin, the final finishing step

phrases.english: They challenged: wooden vessels,
from when do they become susceptible to impurity?
The bed and the crib –
from when he smooths them with fish skin.
phrases.notes: A vessel can only become impure once it is finished. For a bed, the smoothing is the last step.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי מִטָּה מְסוֹרֶגֶת הִיא מֵעַל גַּבָּהּ,
phrases.english: And if a bed is strung over its back,
why do I need smoothing with fish skin?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: כְּלֵי עֵץ, מֵאֵימָתַי מְקַבְּלִין טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's claim that a bed is strung over its back.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that a bed's straps are wrapped over its frame.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires the frame to be smoothed, which only makes sense if the frame shows. That means the straps cannot be covering it.

steps.title: New explanation: both are strung inside
steps.stepSummary: Instead of רבי יוחנן's explanation, both are strung from the inside. A bed's straps pass through holes, while a דרגש's straps pass through loops.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both this and that are strung from the inside. A bed has its straps going in and out through holes; a דרגש has them going in and out through loops.
steps.whatsHappening: Because of the challenge, the גמרא drops רבי יוחנן's explanation and gives a new way to tell a bed from a דרגש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now nothing covers the frame of either one, so smoothing a bed makes sense. The difference moves to how the straps are attached: holes drilled in the bed's frame, or loops on the דרגש.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, which signals that the earlier explanation is being replaced
This and that, meaning both of them

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a defense of רבי יוחנן. The word אלא shows that his explanation is set aside and a different one takes its place.

phrases.english: Rather, both this and that are from the inside:
a bed – they go in and out through holes,
a דרגש – they go in and out through loops.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by replacing רבי יוחנן's definition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A bed's straps wrap over the frame, while a דרגש's are inside.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are strung inside. A bed uses holes and a דרגש uses loops, so a bed's frame shows and needs smoothing.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב reports in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about a mourner's דרגש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: The הלכה is like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical ruling on the earlier disagreement about what a mourner does with a דרגש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said a mourner does not overturn a דרגש. He only loosens its straps and lets it fall by itself. Here that view is made the halacha.

keyTerms.meaning: The halacha follows the view of
The תנא whose view about the דרגש is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, a mourner does not overturn a דרגש. He loosens its straps so it collapses, following רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov said: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The halacha is in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
phrases.notes: This goes back to the earlier ברייתא, where he said a mourner just loosens the דרגש's straps and lets it fall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the definitions are settled, gives the practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A mourner's דרגש is not overturned. Its straps are loosened and it falls on its own.

steps.title: A bed with long posts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בר אמי rules that if a bed has long posts sticking out, the mourner stands it up on its end, and that is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בר אמי said: A bed whose posts stick out, he stands it up, and that is enough for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a related rule about another kind of bed a mourner might have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Overturning a bed with tall posts would not bring it low, because it would rest on the posts. So instead of overturning it, the mourner stands it up on its end, and that is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The tall posts of a bed that hold up a canopy
And that is enough for him

phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov bar Ami said:
A bed whose posts stick out –
he stands it up, and that is enough for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another special case about the mourner's bed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bed with long canopy posts is stood up on its end instead of being overturned.
steps.whatToRemember: For special beds, the mourner does something else instead of overturning them: a דרגש has its straps loosened, and a bed with tall posts is stood up.

steps.title: The king's powers: optional war and making roads
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: the king may go out to a מלחמת הרשות only with the approval of the court of 71. He may break through property to make a road, nobody can stop him, and his road has no size limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The king brings people out to an optional war by the authority of a court of seventy-one. He breaks through to make himself a road, and no one can stop him. The king's road has no fixed size.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, listing special powers of the king and one limit on them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a war that is not required, the king needs the approval of the סנהדרין of 71. Making roads, though, is entirely in his hands. He can break through people's fences, and no one can protest that his road is too wide.

keyTerms.meaning: An optional war, one the Torah does not require
The court of 71, the great סנהדרין

steps.whyThisMatters: The king has broad powers, but starting an optional war still needs the court's approval.

phrases.english: MISHNA: And he brings out to an optional war
phrases.notes: "He" is the king, who this whole part of the משנה is about.

phrases.aramaic: עַל פִּי בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד,
phrases.english: by the authority of a court of seventy-one,
and he breaks through to make himself a road
and no one can stop him.
The king's road has no fixed size,

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹצִיא לְמִלְחֶמֶת הָרְשׁוּת עַל פִּי בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה continues the list of the king's laws.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An optional war needs the approval of the 71. The king may make roads through private property with no limit on their size.

steps.title: The king's share of the spoils
steps.stepSummary: All the people collect the spoils of war and give them to the king, and he takes the first portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the people take spoils and give them to him, and he takes the first portion.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list with how spoils of war are divided when a king is involved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The soldiers do not just keep what they take. Everything is brought to the king, and he chooses his share first.

keyTerms.meaning: The first portion, chosen before anyone else

steps.whatToRemember: The king's powers in this משנה: an optional war needs the approval of the 71, he may make roads without limit, and he gets the first share of the spoils.

phrases.english: And all the people take spoils and give them to him,
and he takes the first portion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה about the king's rights.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spoils are brought to the king, and he takes the first share.

steps.title: We already learned this rule earlier
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the rule about needing the court of 71 for a מלחמת הרשות was already taught earlier in the מסכת.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: We already learned this once before: they do not go out to an optional war except by the decision of a court of seventy-one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges our משנה: why repeat a rule we already learned at the start of the מסכת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה is not supposed to repeat itself for no reason. The rule about a מלחמת הרשות needing the court of 71 already appears on daf 2a, so the גמרא asks why it shows up again here.

keyTerms.meaning: We already learned it (in a משנה)
An optional war, one the Torah does not command
The great court of 71 judges (the סנהדרין גדולה)

phrases.english: GEMARA: We already learned this one time:
They do not bring out the people to an optional war

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל פִּי בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד.
phrases.english: except by the decision of a court of seventy-one.
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה at the very start of the מסכת, on daf 2a.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה's rules (steps 6-7) to the גמרא, and questions why one of those rules is repeated.
steps.kashyaTarget: The repetition of the מלחמת הרשות rule in our משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same rule was already taught on daf 2a, so repeating it here seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Repeated because the משנה lists all the king's laws
steps.stepSummary: Because our משנה gathers every law about the king, it includes the war rule here too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the משנה here taught all the matters of the king, it also taught going out to an optional war.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The rule is repeated so that the list of the king's laws is complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On daf 2a the rule was taught as part of what the court of 71 decides. Here the משנה lists everything about the king, so it includes the war rule again. Each place has its own reason for teaching it.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because (one thing was taught, another came along with it)

phrases.english: Since he taught all the matters of the king,
he also taught bringing out the people to an optional war.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the משנה repeats itself: it is arranged by topic
steps.terutzMaskana: The repetition belongs here because this משנה gathers all the king's laws together.
steps.whatToRemember: An אַיְּידֵי answer means a rule is repeated so that a topic's list is complete. It does not add a new law.

steps.title: שמואל: the king may do everything in the passage
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a king is truly allowed to do everything listed in פרשת מלך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: everything said in the passage of the king, the king is allowed to do.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. שמואל rules that the king's rights listed in the passage in שמואל א are real permissions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שמואל א פרק ח, שמואל warns the people that a king will take their sons, daughters, fields and crops. שמואל the אמורא reads this as a list of real legal rights, so the king may actually do these things.

keyTerms.meaning: The passage about the king (שמואל א פרק ח)
What is said, what is written

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Everything that is said in the passage of the king,
phrases.notes: That's שמואל א chapter 8, where שמואל lists everything a king will take from the people.

phrases.english: a king is permitted to do it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about the king's powers, connected to the משנה's laws of the king.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A king may legally do everything listed in פרשת מלך.

steps.title: רב: the passage was only meant to make the people afraid
steps.stepSummary: רב disagrees and says the passage was written only so the people would fear the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: this passage was said only to frighten them, as it says, 'You shall surely set a king over you,' meaning his fear should be upon you.
steps.whatsHappening: רב argues with שמואל. He says the passage is a warning meant to create fear of the king, not a real list of permissions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב learns from the double wording שׂוֹם תָּשִׂים that a king must be feared. So שמואל's harsh list was meant to scare the people into respecting the king, but the king may not actually do all of it.

keyTerms.meaning: His fear, the fear of him

phrases.english: Rav said:
This passage was not said
except to frighten them,
as it is said: 'You shall surely set a king over you',
phrases.notes: דברים 17:15

phrases.english: meaning that his fear should be upon you.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: לֹא נֶאֶמְרָה פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ אֶלָּא לְאַיֵּים עֲלֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to שמואל's ruling in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פרשת מלך was written to create fear of the king. It does not give him real permission to do everything listed.
steps.confusionAlert: רב does not say the king has no special status. He agrees the king must be feared. He only disagrees about whether the list in שמואל א gives real permissions.

steps.title: The same argument appears among the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יוסי holds like שמואל and רבי יהודה holds like רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like an argument between תנאים: רבי יוסי says everything said in the passage of the king, the king is allowed to do. רבי יהודה says this passage was said only to frighten them, as it says, 'You shall surely set a king over you,' meaning his fear should be upon you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the argument between שמואל and רב is not new. Earlier, the תנאים רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה argued the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says the king may do everything in the passage, just like שמואל. רבי יהודה says it was only meant to frighten the people, using the same פסוק as רב. So each אמורא has a תנא who agrees with him.

keyTerms.meaning: It is like an argument of the תנאים
A תנא who holds like שמואל here
A תנא who holds like רב here

phrases.english: It is like a dispute between Tannaim:
Rabbi Yosei says:
Everything that is said in the passage of the king,
a king is permitted to do it.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
This passage was not said
except in order to frighten them,
as it is said: 'You shall surely set a king over you',
meaning that his fear should be upon you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the אמוראים' dispute from steps 10-11 to an earlier dispute among the תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי holds like שמואל and רבי יהודה holds like רב.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that both opinions have support from the time of the תנאים, so neither אמורא is standing alone.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: three מצוות upon entering the land
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה teaches that ישראל received three מצוות when they entered ארץ ישראל: to appoint a king, to destroy עמלק, and to build the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so רבי יהודה used to say: ישראל were commanded three מצוות when they entered the land: to appoint a king over themselves, to wipe out the seed of עמלק, and to build the Chosen House.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with another teaching of רבי יהודה. It lists three מצוות that began when ישראל entered the land, and appointing a king is the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits רבי יהודה's view that having a king is a real מצוה, not just something allowed. The ברייתא lists the three מצוות here without saying which comes first. רבי יוסי works out the order from פסוקים in steps 17-21.

keyTerms.meaning: To cut off, to wipe out
The Chosen House, the בית המקדש

phrases.english: And so Rabbi Yehuda would say:
Israel was commanded three מצוות
upon their entering the land:
to appoint a king for themselves,
and to cut off the seed of Amalek,
and to build for themselves the Chosen House.
phrases.notes: The 'Chosen House' is the בית המקדש in ירושלים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with another teaching of רבי יהודה, showing that appointing a king is a real מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three מצוות began when ישראל entered the land: appointing a king, wiping out עמלק, and building the בית המקדש.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה, appointing a king is a true מצוה, the first of three that began when ישראל entered the land.

steps.title: רבי נהוראי: The king passage answers the people's complaint
steps.stepSummary: רבי נהוראי says פרשת מלך was said only in response to the people's grumbling. He proves it from the words 'and you will say, I will set a king over me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נהוראי says: This passage was said only because of their complaint, as the פסוק says: 'And you will say: I will set a king over me, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion is added to the debate about פרשת מלך. רבי נהוראי says the passage was a reaction to the people's complaining, not a real command.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes the people demanding a king ('and you will say'). It does not command them. So for רבי נהוראי, appointing a king is not a מצוה. The Torah is only telling us what will happen when they complain, unlike the view in step 13 that it is one of three מצוות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Nehorai says:
This passage was not said
except in response to their complaint,
as it says: 'And you will say: I will set a king over me, etc.'
phrases.notes: דברים 17:14. The פסוק goes on: 'like all the nations around me.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נְהוֹרַאי אוֹמֵר: לֹא נֶאֶמְרָה פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ אֶלָּא כְּנֶגֶד תַּרְעוֹמְתָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with step 13 by denying that appointing a king is a מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פרשת מלך is a response to the people's complaint, not a command to appoint a king.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: The elders asked well, the common people spoiled it
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says the elders properly asked for a king to judge them. The עמי הארץ ruined it by wanting to be like the other nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר says: The elders of that generation asked properly, as it says: 'Give us a king to judge us.' But the unlearned people among them ruined it, as it says: 'That we too may be like all the nations, and our king will judge us and go out before us.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא explains why asking for a king in the days of שמואל was criticized. It splits the people into two groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The elders wanted a king for justice ('to judge us'), and that was a fitting request. The עמי הארץ wanted a king so they could copy the nations, and that was the problem. So the sin was not asking for a king. It was the wrong motive behind the request.
steps.confusionAlert: Both groups asked for a king. The difference is why they asked, not whether they asked.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
The elders of the generation asked properly,
phrases.notes: This is the generation of שמואל הנביא, when the people asked him for a king.

phrases.english: as it says: 'Give us a king to judge us.'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 8:6

phrases.english: But the unlearned people among them ruined it,
as it says: 'That we too may be like all the nations,'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 8:20

phrases.english: 'and our king will judge us and go out before us.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: זְקֵנִים שֶׁבַּדּוֹר כַּהוֹגֶן שָׁאֲלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how a request for a king could be both proper and criticized, which helps fit together the views in steps 13 and 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Asking for a king for justice was proper. Asking in order to imitate the nations was wrong.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: Three מצוות upon entering the land
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי יוסי lists three מצוות for entering ארץ ישראל: appoint a king, wipe out עמלק, and build the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יוסי says: The Jewish people were commanded three מצוות when they entered the land: to appoint a king for themselves, to wipe out the descendants of עמלק, and to build for themselves the Chosen House.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא, this time in the name of רבי יוסי, listing the three מצוות. It sets up the question of which one comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא treats appointing a king as a real מצוה, unlike רבי נהוראי. The list itself is the same three מצוות as in step 13. What is new here is that רבי יוסי goes on to ask about their order.

keyTerms.meaning: The Chosen House, meaning the בית המקדש

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
The Jewish people were commanded three מצוות
when they entered the land:
to appoint a king for themselves,
and to wipe out the descendants of עמלק,
and to build for themselves the Chosen House.
phrases.notes: The 'Chosen House' is the בית המקדש, built in the place ה׳ chose.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: שָׁלֹשׁ מִצְוֹת נִצְטַוּוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּכְנִיסָתָן לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא that repeats the list of three מצוות in order to ask about their order.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Appointing a king, destroying עמלק, and building the בית המקדש are three מצוות tied to entering the land.

steps.title: Which of the three comes first?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says he does not know which of the three מצוות must be done first.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I do not know which of them comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי raises a question about the order of the three מצוות. This is a setup line, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing that all three are required does not tell us the sequence. The question opens a search for a פסוק that shows which one must come first.

phrases.english: But I do not know which of them comes first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the order of the three מצוות listed in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the three מצוות must be done first?

steps.title: The king comes before the war with עמלק
steps.stepSummary: From the פסוק 'a hand upon the throne of ה׳, a war for ה׳ with עמלק,' רבי יוסי learns that the king (the throne) comes first, and then the war with עמלק.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the פסוק says: 'For there is a hand upon the throne of ה׳‎: ה׳ will have war with עמלק,' you must say that they should appoint a king for themselves first.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי answers his own question with a פסוק. The order of the words shows that the throne (a king) comes before the war against עמלק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the throne is mentioned first and the war with עמלק after it. So a king must be appointed first, and then the war against עמלק is fought. This reading only works if 'throne' means a king, and the next step proves that.

keyTerms.meaning: You must say, it follows that

phrases.english: When it says:
'For there is a hand upon the throne of ה׳,'
phrases.notes: שמות 17:16

phrases.english: 'Hashem will have war with עמלק,'
you must say:
to appoint a king for themselves first.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר: ״כִּי יָד עַל כֵּס יָהּ מִלְחָמָה לַה׳ בַּעֲמָלֵק״, הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Appointing a king comes first, before the war with עמלק, because the throne is mentioned before the war in the פסוק.

steps.title: Proof that 'throne' means a king
steps.stepSummary: The word 'throne' in the פסוק refers to a king, as we see from the פסוק 'שלמה sat on the throne of ה׳ as king.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And 'throne' means nothing other than a king, as it says: 'And שלמה sat on the throne of ה׳ as king.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי backs up his reading by proving that 'throne of ה׳' means a king of Israel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 depends on reading 'throne' as a king. A פסוק about שלמה calls a king's throne 'the throne of ה׳.' This confirms that the עמלק פסוק is talking about a king, so the king comes first.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי, appointing a king is a real מצוה, and it must come before the war against עמלק. He learns this from 'כס יה' in the עמלק פסוק, which means a king's throne.

phrases.english: And 'throne' means nothing other than a king,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיֵּשֶׁב שְׁלֹמֹה עַל כִּסֵּא ה׳ לְמֶלֶךְ״.
phrases.english: as it says: 'And שלמה sat on the throne of Hashem as king.'
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 29:23

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 18's reading of 'throne' as a king.
steps.raayaObject: That 'כס' in the עמלק פסוק refers to a king.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים א 29:23: 'And שלמה sat on the throne of ה׳ as king.'

steps.title: Which comes first: the בית המקדש or wiping out עמלק?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי asks which comes next after the king: building the בית הבחירה or wiping out עמלק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I still do not know whether building the בית הבחירה comes first, or wiping out the seed of עמלק comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי already knows the king comes first. Now he asks about the order of the other two מצוות. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 only showed that the king comes before עמלק. It did not say where the בית המקדש fits. So two מצוות are still left to put in order, and רבי יוסי asks which one goes first.

keyTerms.meaning: The Chosen House, meaning the בית המקדש

phrases.english: And I still do not know

phrases.aramaic: אִם לִבְנוֹת לָהֶם בֵּית הַבְּחִירָה תְּחִלָּה,
phrases.english: whether to build them the Chosen House first,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לְהַכְרִית זַרְעוֹ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק תְּחִלָּה.
phrases.english: or to wipe out the seed of עמלק first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up where Step 18 left off. The king is settled, so now he asks about the other two.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether building the בית המקדש or wiping out עמלק comes first, after the king is appointed.

steps.title: Rest from enemies comes before the chosen place
steps.stepSummary: From the פסוק 'He will give you rest from all your enemies… then the place ה׳ will choose', we learn that עמלק is wiped out before the בית המקדש is built.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the פסוק says, 'And He will give you rest from all your enemies… and then the place that ה׳ will choose…', you must say that wiping out עמלק comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי answers his question from a פסוק in דברים. The פסוק mentions rest from enemies first, and only after that the chosen place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order of the פסוק shows the order of the מצוות. First there is rest from all enemies, which includes wiping out עמלק. Only after that does the פסוק speak about 'the place ה׳ will choose', meaning the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: And He will give you rest
The place that ה׳ will choose (the בית המקדש)
You must say / it must be that

steps.whatToRemember: Full order according to רבי יוסי: (1) appoint a king, (2) wipe out עמלק, (3) build the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: When it says:
"And He will give you rest from all your enemies, etc.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיָה הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר ה׳ וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: and then the place that ה׳ will choose, etc."
you must say:
wiping out the seed of עמלק comes first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Wiping out עמלק comes before building the בית המקדש, because the פסוק puts rest from enemies before the chosen place.

steps.title: דוד wanted to build only after he had rest
steps.stepSummary: The story of דוד המלך supports the order: only once ה׳ gave him rest from his enemies did he start talking about building a house for ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too it says about דוד: 'When King דוד sat in his house and ה׳ had given him rest all around', and then it is written: 'The king said to נתן the prophet: See, I live in a house of cedar…'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings support from נביא. דוד first had rest from his enemies, and only afterward did he want to build the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two פסוקים come one right after the other. First comes the rest from enemies, and then comes דוד's plan to build a house for the ארון. That matches the order learned in Step 21: wars first, then the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: And so too concerning דוד it says:
"And it was when King דוד sat in his house
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 7:1

phrases.english: and ה׳ had given him rest all around,"
and it is written:
"The king said to נתן the prophet:
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 7:2

phrases.aramaic: רְאֵה נָא אָנֹכִי יוֹשֵׁב בְּבֵית אֲרָזִים וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: See now, I live in a house of cedar, etc."
phrases.notes: The rest of the פסוק says the ארון is only under curtains, so דוד wants to build a proper home for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the answer in Step 21 with a real story from נביא.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that wiping out the enemies comes before building the בית המקדש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל ב 7:1–2: דוד had rest from his enemies, and right after that he spoke of building a house for ה׳.

steps.title: שלמה first ruled above, later only below
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש teaches that שלמה at first ruled even over the upper worlds, and in the end ruled only over the lower world.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: At first שלמה ruled over the upper worlds, as it says, 'שלמה sat on the throne of ה׳'. In the end he ruled over the lower world, as it says, 'For he ruled over all the region across the river, from תפסח to עזה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about שלמה's kingdom. It ties in to the פסוק 'שלמה sat on the throne of ה׳' from Step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The throne of ה׳' shows that שלמה's rule was like ה׳'s rule, reaching even the upper worlds. A later פסוק describes his rule only by places on earth. That shows his kingdom became smaller.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, partner in learning of רבי יוחנן
The lower world / beings on earth

phrases.english: ריש לקיש said:
At first שלמה ruled over the upper ones,
as it says: "And שלמה sat on the throne of Hashem,"
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 29:23. This is the same פסוק used back in Step 19.

phrases.english: and in the end he ruled over the lower ones,
as it says:
"For he ruled over all the region across the river,
phrases.notes: מלכים א 5:4

phrases.english: from תפסח to עזה."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the פסוק about שלמה's throne from Step 19 and starts a new topic about his kingdom.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלמה's kingdom shrank: at first it reached the upper worlds, and later only the lower world.

steps.title: רב and שמואל: where were תפסח and עזה?
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל disagree about the meaning of 'from תפסח to עזה'. Either these are the two far ends of the world, or they are two neighboring places that stand for the whole world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל: One says, 'תפסח is at one end of the world and עזה is at the other end.' The other says, 'תפסח and עזה were right next to each other, and just as he ruled over תפסח and עזה, so he ruled over the entire world.'
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים explain the פסוק from Step 23 in two different ways. Both agree that שלמה ruled over the whole lower world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view reads 'from תפסח to עזה' as from one end of the world to the other. The second view says the two towns were next to each other. So the פסוק cannot be measuring distance. It must be saying that he ruled the whole world just as surely as he ruled these two towns.

keyTerms.meaning: At the end of the world

steps.whatToRemember: Both views agree that שלמה ruled the whole lower world. They only disagree about how the words 'from תפסח to עזה' show it.

phrases.english: רב and שמואל:
phrases.notes: The גמרא doesn't tell us which of them holds which view.

phrases.english: One says,
"תפסח is at the end of the world
and עזה is at the end of the world,"
and one says,
"תפסח and עזה were located next to each other,"

phrases.aramaic: וּכְשֵׁם שֶׁמָּלַךְ עַל תִּפְסַח וְעַל עַזָּה
phrases.english: and just as he ruled over תפסח and over עזה,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ מָלַךְ עַל כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ.
phrases.english: so he ruled over the entire world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the words 'from תפסח to עזה' in the פסוק quoted by ריש לקיש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Either תפסח and עזה are the two ends of the world, or they are two neighboring towns, and the פסוק teaches that שלמה ruled the whole world just as he ruled them.

steps.title: שלמה keeps falling, step by step, until he rules only his staff
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש continues: שלמה ruled over ישראל, then only ירושלים, then only his bed, and finally only his staff. Each stage has a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end he ruled only over ישראל, as it says: 'I, קהלת, was king over ישראל.' Later he ruled only over ירושלים, as it says: 'The words of קהלת, son of דוד, king in ירושלים.' Later he ruled only over his bed, as it says: 'Behold the bed of שלמה.' Finally he ruled only over his staff, as it says: 'This was my portion from all my labor.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues ריש לקיש's teaching from Step 23 and lists each smaller stage of שלמה's fall, with a פסוק for every stage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק describes שלמה ruling over something smaller than the one before. The ladder goes down from ישראל, to ירושלים, to his bed, to his staff. In the last פסוק, the word 'this' is read as pointing to the one small thing he had left.

keyTerms.meaning: And in the end, and then later
A name for שלמה used in ספר קהלת

phrases.aramaic: וּלְבַסּוֹף לֹא מָלַךְ אֶלָּא עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: And in the end he ruled only over Israel,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אֲנִי קֹהֶלֶת הָיִיתִי מֶלֶךְ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: as it is said: 'I, Koheleth, was king over Israel, etc.'
phrases.notes: קהלת 1:12

phrases.aramaic: וּלְבַסּוֹף לֹא מָלַךְ אֶלָּא עַל יְרוּשָׁלַיִם,
phrases.english: And later he ruled only over Jerusalem,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״דִּבְרֵי קֹהֶלֶת בֶּן דָּוִד מֶלֶךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָים״.
phrases.english: as it is said: 'The words of Koheleth, son of David, king in Jerusalem.'
phrases.notes: קהלת 1:1

phrases.aramaic: וּלְבַסּוֹף, לֹא מָלַךְ אֶלָּא עַל מִטָּתוֹ,
phrases.english: And later he ruled only over his bed,
as it is said: 'Behold, the bed of Solomon, etc.'
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 3:7

phrases.aramaic: וּלְבַסּוֹף לֹא מָלַךְ אֶלָּא עַל מַקְלוֹ,
phrases.english: And finally he ruled only over his staff,
as it is said: 'This was my portion from all my labor.'
phrases.notes: קהלת 2:10. The word 'this' points to the one small thing he had left.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְבַסּוֹף לֹא מָלַךְ אֶלָּא עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up ריש לקיש's statement from Step 23 after the side discussion in Step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלמה's rule shrank stage by stage until all he had was his staff.

steps.title: Was 'this' his staff or his cloak?
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל disagree about what 'this' means in the last פסוק. One says it was his staff and one says it was his cloak.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל: one said 'this' means his staff, and the other said it means his cloak.
steps.whatsHappening: רב and שמואל argue about which object the word 'this' points to in the last פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that שלמה was left with only one small personal item. They disagree only about which item it was: a staff or a cloak.

keyTerms.meaning: One said (used when we don't know which רב said which view)

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel: one said 'his staff,'
and one said 'his cloak.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the last פסוק of Step 25 in more detail.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The one item שלמה was left with was either his staff or his cloak.

steps.title: Did שלמה ever get his kingdom back?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether שלמה went back to being king after his fall.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did he return to his kingship or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question: after falling so low, did שלמה ever become king again? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 23 and 25 described only the fall. This question asks how the story ends, whether he stayed low or rose again.

phrases.english: Did he return, or did he not return?
phrases.notes: Did שלמה go back to ruling as king?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the story of שלמה's fall and asks how it ended.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether שלמה regained his kingdom after his fall.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree whether he returned
steps.stepSummary: One says שלמה returned and one says he did not. In one view his story was king, then commoner. In the other it was king, then commoner, then king again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל: one said he returned, and one said he did not. The one who says he did not return holds that he was a king and then a commoner. The one who says he returned holds that he was a king, then a commoner, and then a king again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a disagreement between רב and שמואל, and then lays out each side's version of שלמה's life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that שלמה became a הדיוט at some point. The only argument is whether the story ends there or ends with him as king again.

keyTerms.meaning: A regular person, a commoner, not a king

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel: one said he returned,
and one said he did not return.
The one who says he did not return:
king, then commoner;
and the one who says he returned:
king, then commoner, then king again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a dispute: one view says שלמה ended as a commoner, the other says he became king again.
steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש teaches that שלמה fell from ruling over the upper worlds all the way down to owning only his staff or cloak. רב and שמואל disagree whether he ever became king again.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: the king's share of war spoils
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that a king may break through to make a road. Then it brings a ברייתא: treasures of conquered kings go to the king, and other spoils are split half to the king and half to the people.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says the king may break through to make a road for himself. The Rabbis taught: treasures of kings go to the king, and the rest of the spoils that are taken are half for the king and half for the people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the story of שלמה and goes back to the משנה's list of a king's rights. It quotes the next line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא about another right, the king's share of war spoils.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא splits spoils into two groups. Treasures that belonged to enemy kings go entirely to our king. All other loot is divided equally between the king and the people.

keyTerms.meaning: Breaks through, breaches a fence or wall

phrases.english: He breaks through to make a road for himself.
The Rabbis taught:
Treasures of kings go to the king,
and the rest of the spoils that are taken:
half for the king and half for the people.

steps.triggerLanguage: פּוֹרֵץ לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ דֶּרֶךְ. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story of שלמה and returns to explaining the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Treasures of enemy kings belong to the king; other spoils are split half to the king and half to the people.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for a connection between this ברייתא and the stories about שלמה. The גמרא has simply gone back to the משנה's list of a king's rights.

steps.title: אביי asks: what is the source for the half-and-half split?
steps.stepSummary: אביי accepts that kings' treasures go to the king, since that is just natural. He asks where we learn that the king gets half of the ordinary spoils.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב דימי, and some say to רב אחא: It makes sense that the treasures of kings go to the king; that is the normal way of things. But that the rest of the spoils are half for the king and half for the people, where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks for a source for the second rule of the ברייתא, the half-and-half split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first rule needs no source because it is natural for a king to take another king's treasures. Giving the king half of everyone's ordinary loot is not obvious, so אביי wants to know where it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (a different version of who was involved)
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Dimi,
and some say it was to Rav Acha:
It makes sense that treasures of kings go to the king;
that is the normal way of things.
But the rest of the spoils that are taken,
half for the king and half for the people,
from where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the second rule in the ברייתא of Step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that the king gets half of the ordinary war spoils.

steps.title: The answer begins: 'As it is written'
steps.stepSummary: The answer to אביי starts by introducing a פסוק. The פסוק itself comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written:
steps.whatsHappening: This is the opening word of the answer. It tells us a פסוק is about to be quoted as the source, so the גמרא is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer will come from a פסוק, not from logic. The actual פסוק and how it proves the half-and-half split come right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: As it is written:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering אביי's question from Step 30.
